key_insight: Neural surrogates trained on quantum-hardware samples accelerated autocorrelation decay in constrained Boltzmann sampling with more than 1,000 binary variables.
engineering_relevance: A divide-and-conquer implementation extends quantum-assisted sampling to large systems by using neural surrogates for quantum-generated proposals.
method: Generate QAOA training samples on an IBM Quantum Heron r2 processor.
Train neural surrogates for quantum-enhanced MCMC.
Use divide-and-conquer subproblems to support larger systems.
evidence_signal: Experiments covered N=144 and N=1064; at N=1064, autocorrelation decay per MCMC step was approximately 5.2× and 12.3× faster than global and local Kawasaki dynamics, respectively.
watch_item: Larger subproblems challenged neural-surrogate learning, and faster decay per MCMC step does not establish an end-to-end runtime advantage.
paper_title: Hardware Demonstration of Neural-Surrogated Quantum-Enhanced MCMC for Large-Scale Constrained Boltzmann Sampling
